description_short.value: London-based oil and gas producer focused on Ghana's offshore Jubilee and TEN fields, listed in London and on the Ghana Stock Exchange.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Tullow Oil plc 2025 Full Year Results (GSE PR 167/2026) and the notes to editors in its GSE announcements (e.g. PR 449/2025)

description_full.value: Tullow Oil plc is an independent oil and gas company incorporated in England and Wales and based in London. Its production now comes from Ghana, chiefly the offshore Jubilee and TEN fields. It has sold its other producing and development assets: it sold its Gabon assets to the Gabon Oil Company for US$307 million net of tax in July 2025, and its Kenya interests to an affiliate of Gulf Energy in September 2025 for at least US$120 million. Its shares are quoted in London and, since July 2011, on the Ghana Stock Exchange. It reports in US dollars. Revenue fell from US$1.78 billion in 2022 to US$847 million in 2025, partly because Gabon is now reported as a discontinued operation. Profit for the year swung between losses and small profits (US$6.5 million in 2025). Its liabilities have exceeded its assets throughout 2021 to 2025 (net liabilities of US$253 million at the end of 2025), and it has paid no dividend in that period. In April 2026 it completed a refinancing, backed by over 99% of bondholders and Glencore, that replaced its 2026 notes with notes due in 2028 and its Glencore loan with junior notes due in 2030. The 2028 notes fall due earlier, in May 2028, unless a sale agreement for its assets is signed by 30 September 2027. First-half 2026 working-interest production was 43.7 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day. Ian Perks became Chief Executive in September 2025, and Roald Goethe became Chair in December 2025, when the board was cut back.
